entries.title: An attacker pulls about 350 ETH from Float Protocol's Rari Capital pool
entries.body: Lack of liquidity in the Uniswap V3 FLOAT/USDC oracle allowed an attacker to manipulate the prices within the pool, then deposit it at a much higher rate. The hacker pulled about 350 ETH (equivalent to $1.1 million) out of the pool, though according to PeckShield they later returned around $250,000 for some reason.

entries.body: Crypto investors who bought 40 acres of land in Wyoming in hopes of "building a city on the Ethereum blockchain" lost more than $92,000 to a Discord hack. Some clever social engineering and questionable security measures on Discord's part allowed scammers to gain control of a CityDAO Discord moderator's account, then send out fake announcements about a fake "land <button class="define-target" id="airdrop">drop</button>". The scammer received over 29.67 ETH (about $92,000).

entries.title: Sports NFT platform Lympo loses $18.7 million to a breach
entries.body: Animoca Brands' subsidiary Lympo, an NFT platform specifically for sports, experienced a breach of several <button class="define-target" id="hot-wallet">hot wallets</button>. This allowed an attacker to pull 165.2 LMT tokens from the platform, equivalent to about $18.7 million. The tokens were quickly exchanged for Ether on Uniswap and Sushiswap. The hack caused the value of LMT to drop by 92%, to $0.0093.

links.linkText: "Animoca Brands’ Lympo NFT platform hacked for $18.7 million"

entries.title: $6.8 million emptied from crypto exchange LCX
entries.body: The Liechtenstein-based cryptocurrency exchange LCX suffered a $6.8 million loss when one of its <button class="define-target" id="hot-wallet">hot wallets</button> was compromised. Assets including ETH, USDC, EURe, and LCX were moved to an Ethereum wallet belonging to the attacker, then quickly <button class="define-target" id="tumbler">tumbled</button> using the Tornado Cash mixing service.

links.linkText: "LCX loses $6.8M in a hot wallet compromise over Ethereum blockchain"

entries.title: Some of Tinyman's liquidity pools are drained of around $3 million
entries.body: Tinyman, a <button class="define-target" id="defi">defi</button> platform that bills itself as "decentralized, secure trading", had all liquidity drained from its goBTC and goETH <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">pools</button> after an attacker found a bug in their <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">smart contracts</button>. Liquidity throughout Tinyman dropped from about $43 million to around $20 million within hours of the attack, though the platform says they believe that most of this money was withdrawn by its rightful owners and not stolen. Tinyman asked users to remove liquidity from all pools while they work to patch their smart contracts, and announced they would reimburse affected users.

entries.title: NFT collector scammed out of $2.2 million in a phishing attack

links.linkText: "Bored Ape NFT Collector Loses $2.2M in Phishing Scam"
'All My Apes Gone': NFT Theft Victims Beg for Centralized Saviors

entries.body:
Todd Kramer, an NFT collector who had acquired Bored Ape and other pricey NFTs, clicked on a phishing that appeared to be a legitimate NFT trader link. Sixteen NFTs from three collections were taken, including eight Bored Ape NFTs. In total, the loss totalled around 593 ETH (equivalent to about $2.2 million).

"I been hacked. all my apes gone." tweeted Kramer, in a phrase that ultimately became a catchphrase of the NFT world (and its critics).

After asking for help on Twitter, OpenSea the stolen assets, preventing them from being traded on their platform. Some commenters noted that the redress (asset freezing and flagging of suspicious accounts) was only possible because OpenSea is a centralized platform with a large amount of power in the NFT arena, which some see as antithetical to the supposed ideals of web3. This also raises the question of whether BAYC themselves have a way to determine "legitimate ownership" of their NFTs, which in addition to being expensive status symbols also grant their owners exclusive perks including merchandising rights and access to events.

p>

entries.title: Blatant copy of Solana's popular "Baby Ape Social Club" rakes in more than $50,000 before being taken down by OpenSea
entries.body: A clone of Solana's popular "Baby Ape Social Club" project popped up on OpenSea, using the Polygon blockchain. The project enjoyed 14.3 ETH in trading volume (about $52,000) before OpenSea finally took them down.

entries.title: Traders duped out of $1.8 million in a fake MetaMask governance token scheme
entries.body: Scammers took advantage of rumors that MetaMask, a popular Ethereum <button class="define-target" id="wallet">wallet</button>, would be <button class="define-target" id="airdrop">airdropping</button> <button class="define-target" id="governance-token">governance tokens</button>. The scammers created a fake MetaMask token, $MASK, and managed to inject code into the popular DEXTools trading app to show the token as verified. The token reached over $9 million in traded volume before scammers pulled the <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">liquidity</button>, making off with about $1.8 million worth of Ethereum.

They popped up in my wallet, I clicked on it to delete it, immediately they stole 19 grand. Happily I just started this wallet, they already stole 19,000 out of it. I need fucking help immediately."

The project creators took the invested tokens and quickly <button class="define-target" id="tumbler">tumbled</button> them using Tornado Cash.
